1	"""Named branches over a shared event graph."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import heapq
6	import itertools
7	import math
8	from typing import Any
9	
10	from city_twin.event_graph import EventGraph
11	
12	
13	class BranchStore:
14	    """Named heads into a shared :class:`EventGraph`.
15	
16	    A branch is created from an existing event and grows only by appending
17	    events whose sole parent is the branch's current head, so branches
18	    never move each other's heads. Appends are idempotent: the store
19	    records the ``(at, changes)`` each branch appended under an event id,
20	    and repeating the same call is a no-op. All validation finishes before
21	    any state is touched, so a failed call leaves the graph, branch heads
22	    and idempotency records unchanged.
23	    """
24	
25	    def __init__(self, graph: EventGraph) -> None:
26	        if not isinstance(graph, EventGraph):
27	            raise TypeError(
28	                f"graph must be an EventGraph, got {type(graph).__name__}"
29	            )
30	        self._graph = graph
31	        self._heads: dict[str, str] = {}
32	        self._sources: dict[str, str] = {}
33	        self._appends: dict[str, dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, int]]]] = {}
34	        self._merges: dict[str, tuple[str, str, int, dict[str, int]]] = {}
35	
36	    @staticmethod
37	    def _require_nonempty_str(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
38	        # Same contract as EventGraph.add's string parameters.
39	        EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(value, name)
40	
41	    def _require_known_branch(self, name: str) -> None:
42	        if name not in self._heads:
43	            raise KeyError(name)
44	
45	    def create(self, name: str, from_event: str) -> None:
46	        """Create a branch named ``name`` starting at ``from_event``.
47	
48	        Re-creating with the same name and source is a no-op; the same
49	        name with a different source is a conflict.
50	        """
51	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
52	        self._require_nonempty_str(from_event, "from_event")
53	
54	        if name in self._heads:
55	            if self._sources[name] != from_event:
56	                raise ValueError(
57	                    f"branch {name!r} already exists from "
58	                    f"{self._sources[name]!r}, not {from_event!r}"
59	                )
60	            return
61	        if from_event not in self._graph._at:
62	            raise KeyError(from_event)
63	
64	        self._heads[name] = from_event
65	        self._sources[name] = from_event
66	        self._appends[name] = {}
67	
68	    def append(
69	        self,
70	        name: str,
71	        id: str,
72	        at: int,
73	        changes: dict[str, int],
74	    ) -> None:
75	        """Append an event whose sole parent is the branch's current head.
76	
77	        The head moves only if :meth:`EventGraph.add` succeeds. Repeating
78	        an append with the same ``name``/``id``/``at``/``changes`` is a
79	        no-op; reusing ``id`` with different inputs is a conflict, here
80	        and via the graph across branches.
81	        """
82	        # --- Full validation happens before any state is consulted. ---
83	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
84	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
85	        # The at/changes contract is exactly EventGraph.add's.
86	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
87	        if at_value < 0:
88	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
89	        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
90	            raise TypeError(
91	                f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}"
92	            )
93	        for key, value in changes.items():
94	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
95	            EventGraph._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
96	        # Copy caller-owned input before it can be recorded anywhere.
97	        changes = dict(changes)
98	
99	        self._require_known_branch(name)
100	
101	        recorded = self._appends[name].get(id)
102	        if recorded is not None:
103	            if recorded == (at_value, changes):
104	                return
105	            raise ValueError(
106	                f"event {id!r} already appended on branch {name!r} "
107	                f"with different inputs"
108	            )
109	
110	        head = self._heads[name]
111	        self._graph.add(id, at_value, (head,), changes)
112	
113	        # --- Commit: only after the graph accepted the event. ---
114	        self._heads[name] = id
115	        self._appends[name][id] = (at_value, changes)
116	
117	    def merge(
118	        self,
119	        target: str,
120	        source: str,
121	        id: str,
122	        at: int,
123	        changes: dict[str, int],
124	    ) -> None:
125	        """Merge ``source`` into ``target`` under a new two-parent event.
126	
127	        The event's parents are ordered ``(target head, source head)``;
128	        only the target head moves, the source head is untouched. Calls
129	        are idempotent on the exact five-tuple, and reusing ``id`` with
130	        different inputs (here or in the graph) is a conflict. A merge is
131	        rejected when events exclusive to either side touch overlapping
132	        change keys. All validation finishes before any state is touched,
133	        so a failed call leaves the graph, heads and records unchanged.
134	        """
135	        # --- Full validation happens before any state is consulted. ---
136	        self._require_nonempty_str(target, "target")
137	        self._require_nonempty_str(source, "source")
138	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
139	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
140	        if at_value < 0:
141	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
142	        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
143	            raise TypeError(
144	                f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}"
145	            )
146	        for key, value in changes.items():
147	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
148	            EventGraph._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
149	        # Copy caller-owned input before it can be recorded anywhere.
150	        changes = dict(changes)
151	
152	        self._require_known_branch(target)
153	        self._require_known_branch(source)
154	        if target == source:
155	            raise ValueError(f"cannot merge branch {target!r} into itself")
156	
157	        recorded = self._merges.get(id)
158	        if recorded is not None:
159	            if recorded == (target, source, at_value, changes):
160	                return
161	            raise ValueError(
162	                f"merge event {id!r} already recorded with different inputs"
163	            )
164	
165	        target_head = self._heads[target]
166	        source_head = self._heads[source]
167	
168	        target_closure = set(self._graph._ordered_ancestors(target_head))
169	        source_closure = set(self._graph._ordered_ancestors(source_head))
170	        common = target_closure & source_closure
171	
172	        target_keys: set[str] = set()
173	        for event_id in target_closure - common:
174	            target_keys.update(self._graph._changes[event_id])
175	        source_keys: set[str] = set()
176	        for event_id in source_closure - common:
177	            source_keys.update(self._graph._changes[event_id])
178	        overlap = target_keys & source_keys
179	        if overlap:
180	            raise ValueError(
181	                "conflicting changes on keys: "
182	                + ", ".join(sorted(overlap))
183	            )
184	
185	        self._graph.add(id, at_value, (target_head, source_head), changes)
186	
187	        # --- Commit: only after the graph accepted the event. ---
188	        self._heads[target] = id
189	        self._merges[id] = (target, source, at_value, changes)
190	
191	    def audit_merge(self, id: str) -> dict[str, object]:
192	        """Return an audit record for the merge event ``id``.
193	
194	        The record is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
195	        ``event_id, target, source, parents, at, changes``: the merge
196	        event id, the target and source branch names, the recorded
197	        parent ids (target head first), the non-negative timestamp and
198	        a copy of the merged changes. Unknown ids and ids of non-merge
199	        events raise :class:`KeyError`; mutating the returned dict or
200	        its ``changes`` never affects the store's records.
201	        """
202	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
203	        recorded = self._merges.get(id)
204	        if recorded is None:
205	            raise KeyError(id)
206	        target, source, at_value, changes = recorded
207	        return {
208	            "event_id": id,
209	            "target": target,
210	            "source": source,
211	            "parents": self._graph._parents[id],
212	            "at": at_value,
213	            "changes": dict(changes),
214	        }
215	
216	    def audit_log(self) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
217	        """Return audit records for every event this store recorded.
218	
219	        Covers exactly the branch appends and merges performed through
220	        this store -- events added directly to the graph are not
221	        included -- each exactly once, ordered by ``(at, event_id)``
222	        ascending (event ids compared by Unicode code point). Each
223	        record is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
224	        ``event_id, kind, owner, peer, parents, at, changes``: for an
225	        append, ``owner`` is the branch name, ``peer`` is ``None`` and
226	        ``parents`` is the single-element parent id tuple; for a merge,
227	        ``owner`` is the target branch, ``peer`` is the source branch
228	        and ``parents`` is the two-element tuple with the target parent
229	        first. ``changes`` is a copy ordered by Unicode code point of
230	        its keys. The query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and
231	        records are never modified, and the returned tuple, dicts and
232	        changes are detached from internal state, so mutating them
233	        affects neither the store nor later calls, and repeated calls
234	        return item-wise equal results in a stable order.
235	        """
236	        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
237	        for name, appends in self._appends.items():
238	            for event_id, (at_value, changes) in appends.items():
239	                records.append(
240	                    {
241	                        "event_id": event_id,
242	                        "kind": "append",
243	                        "owner": name,
244	                        "peer": None,
245	                        "parents": self._graph._parents[event_id],
246	                        "at": at_value,
247	                        "changes": {
248	                            key: changes[key] for key in sorted(changes)
249	                        },
250	                    }
251	                )
252	        for event_id, (target, source, at_value, changes) in (
253	            self._merges.items()
254	        ):
255	            records.append(
256	                {
257	                    "event_id": event_id,
258	                    "kind": "merge",
259	                    "owner": target,
260	                    "peer": source,
261	                    "parents": self._graph._parents[event_id],
262	                    "at": at_value,
263	                    "changes": {
264	                        key: changes[key] for key in sorted(changes)
265	                    },
266	                }
267	            )
268	        records.sort(
269	            key=lambda record: (record["at"], record["event_id"])
270	        )
271	        return tuple(records)
272	
273	    def trace(self, name: str, key: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
274	        """Return ids of events on ``name``'s head closure touching ``key``.
275	
276	        Ids follow the graph's replay order and include zero-delta and
277	        merge events, each at most once.
278	        """
279	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
280	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
281	        self._require_known_branch(name)
282	        return self._graph.explain(self._heads[name], key)
283	
284	    def explain_change(
285	        self, name: str, key: str
286	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
287	        """Explain the causal value trajectory of ``key`` on a branch.
288	
289	        The branch's current head ancestor closure is replayed in the
290	        graph's parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` order. Every event
291	        whose changes contain ``key`` -- including zero-delta and merge
292	        events -- appears exactly once, with the key's integer value
293	        accumulated from an initial ``0``. Each record is a fresh dict
294	        whose keys are ordered ``event_id, at, parents, delta, before,
295	        after``: the event id, its non-negative timestamp, a copy of its
296	        recorded parent ids (for a merge, target head first, source head
297	        second), the integer delta the event applies to ``key`` and the
298	        values immediately before and after applying it. ``name`` and
299	        ``key`` are validated (in that order) before the branch is looked
300	        up: non-``str`` values raise :class:`TypeError`, empty strings
301	        raise :class:`ValueError`, unknown branches raise
302	        :class:`KeyError`. The query is read-only and its result is
303	        detached from internal state, so the graph, branch heads, audit
304	        and idempotency records are never modified, and repeated calls
305	        return item-wise equal results.
306	        """
307	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
308	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
309	        self._require_known_branch(name)
310	
311	        order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name])
312	        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
313	        value = 0
314	        for event_id in order:
315	            changes = self._graph._changes[event_id]
316	            if key not in changes:
317	                continue
318	            delta = changes[key]
319	            before = value
320	            value += delta
321	            records.append(
322	                {
323	                    "event_id": event_id,
324	                    "at": self._graph._at[event_id],
325	                    "parents": (*self._graph._parents[event_id],),
326	                    "delta": delta,
327	                    "before": before,
328	                    "after": value,
329	                }
330	            )
331	        return tuple(records)
332	
333	    def explain_impact(
334	        self, name: str, event_id: str
335	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
336	        """Explain the forward causal impact of an event on a branch.
337	
338	        Within the ancestor closure of the branch's current head, edges
339	        point parent-to-child as the impact direction. The strict
340	        descendants of ``event_id`` -- reachable events other than
341	        ``event_id`` itself -- are returned each exactly once, in the
342	        graph's parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` order. Each record
343	        is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered ``event_id, at, path,
344	        keys``: the descendant id, its non-negative timestamp, the tuple
345	        of ids on the shortest path from ``event_id`` to it (both ends
346	        included), and the tuple of change keys its ``changes`` touch,
347	        sorted by Unicode code point (an empty tuple for events with no
348	        changes). When several paths exist, the one with the fewest edges
349	        wins, ties broken by the Unicode code point order of the complete
350	        id tuples; no descendants yields an empty tuple. ``name`` and
351	        ``event_id`` are validated (in that order) before the branch is
352	        looked up: non-``str`` values raise :class:`TypeError`, empty
353	        strings raise :class:`ValueError`, unknown branches raise
354	        :class:`KeyError`, and an ``event_id`` absent from the graph or
355	        outside the branch's current head ancestor closure raises
356	        :class:`KeyError`. The query is read-only and its result is
357	        detached from internal state, so the graph, branch heads, audit
358	        and idempotency records are never modified, and repeated calls
359	        return item-wise equal results.
360	        """
361	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
362	        self._require_nonempty_str(event_id, "event_id")
363	        self._require_known_branch(name)
364	        if event_id not in self._graph._at:
365	            raise KeyError(event_id)
366	
367	        head = self._heads[name]
368	        order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(head)
369	        closure = set(order)
370	        if event_id not in closure:
371	            raise KeyError(event_id)
372	
373	        # Reverse the parent edges within the closure so children can be
374	        # enumerated parent-to-child.
375	        children: dict[str, list[str]] = {event: [] for event in closure}
376	        for current in closure:
377	            for parent in self._graph._parents[current]:
378	                children[parent].append(current)
379	
380	        # Level-by-level breadth-first search gives the fewest-edge
381	        # paths. Within a level every candidate path has equal length, so
382	        # keeping the minimum full id tuple applies the Unicode code
383	        # point tie-break; children are claimed only after the whole
384	        # level is evaluated, so every shortest candidate is compared.
385	        paths: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {event_id: (event_id,)}
386	        frontier = [event_id]
387	        while frontier:
388	            candidates: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
389	            for current in frontier:
390	                current_path = paths[current]
391	                for child in children[current]:
392	                    if child in paths:
393	                        continue
394	                    candidate = (*current_path, child)
395	                    best = candidates.get(child)
396	                    if best is None or candidate < best:
397	                        candidates[child] = candidate
398	            for child, path in candidates.items():
399	                paths[child] = path
400	            frontier = list(candidates)
401	
402	        # Descendants are reported in the closure's existing replay
403	        # order: parents before children, ready events by (at, id).
404	        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
405	        for descendant in order:
406	            if descendant == event_id or descendant not in paths:
407	                continue
408	            changes = self._graph._changes[descendant]
409	            records.append(
410	                {
411	                    "event_id": descendant,
412	                    "at": self._graph._at[descendant],
413	                    "path": (*paths[descendant],),
414	                    "keys": tuple(sorted(changes)),
415	                }
416	            )
417	        return tuple(records)

440	    def compare(self, name_a: str, name_b: str) -> dict[str, object]:
441	        """Compare the ancestor closures of two branches' current heads.
442	
443	        Both names are validated (in signature order) before either
444	        branch is looked up: non-``str`` names raise :class:`TypeError`,
445	        empty names raise :class:`ValueError`, unknown branches raise
446	        :class:`KeyError`, and comparing a branch with itself raises
447	        :class:`ValueError`. Each head's ancestor closure is taken once,
448	        in the graph's parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` replay
449	        order. The result is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
450	        ``common, left_only, right_only, fork``: tuples of event ids for
451	        the intersection, the left-only and the right-only events
452	        (common and left-only in left replay order, right-only in right
453	        replay order), plus ``fork`` -- the last common id in left replay
454	        order, or ``None`` when the closures share no event. The query
455	        is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are never
456	        modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached from
457	        internal state.
458	        """
459	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
460	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
461	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
462	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
463	        if name_a == name_b:
464	            raise ValueError(f"cannot compare branch {name_a!r} with itself")
465	
466	        left_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
467	        right_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
468	        left_ids = set(left_order)
469	        right_ids = set(right_order)
470	
471	        common = tuple(
472	            event_id for event_id in left_order if event_id in right_ids
473	        )
474	        left_only = tuple(
475	            event_id for event_id in left_order if event_id not in right_ids
476	        )
477	        right_only = tuple(
478	            event_id for event_id in right_order if event_id not in left_ids
479	        )
480	        return {
481	            "common": common,
482	            "left_only": left_only,
483	            "right_only": right_only,
484	            "fork": common[-1] if common else None,
485	        }

488	        self, name_a: str, name_b: str, key: str

495	        unknown branches raise :class:`KeyError` (``name_a`` first), and

514	        code point order of the complete id tuples, and ``affected`` is
515	        the tuple of the cause's strict descendant ids in that side's
516	        replay order; both are empty tuples when the cause is ``None``.
517	        The query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are
518	        never modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached
519	        from internal state.

523	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
524	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
525	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
526	        if name_a == name_b:
527	            raise ValueError(
528	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
529	                "against itself"
530	            )

532	        return self._attribute_divergence_for(
533	            self._heads[name_a], self._heads[name_b], key

540	        name_b: str,

574	        ties broken by the Unicode code point order of the complete id

576	        descendant ids within that side's closure in its replay order;
577	        both are empty tuples when the cause is ``None``. The query is
578	        read-only: success or failure never modifies the graph, branch
579	        heads, audit or idempotency records, and the returned dict and
580	        tuples are detached from internal state.

584	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
585	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_b, "node_b")

600	        ):

602	        if node_b not in self._graph._at:

611	    def attribute_divergences_at(
612	        self,
613	        name_a: str,
614	        node_a: str,
615	        name_b: str,
616	        node_b: str,
617	        keys: tuple[str, ...],
618	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
619	        """Attribute divergences for several keys at two historical nodes.
620	
621	        The multi-key form of :meth:`attribute_divergence_at`: all five
622	        parameters are validated before either node is replayed. The four
623	        string parameters are checked in signature order (``name_a``,
624	        ``node_a``, ``name_b``, ``node_b``): non-``str`` values raise
625	        :class:`TypeError` and empty strings raise :class:`ValueError`.
626	        ``keys`` must be a tuple (else :class:`TypeError`); its elements
627	        are checked in input order, and a non-``str`` element raises
628	        :class:`TypeError`, while an empty or duplicated key raises
629	        :class:`ValueError`. The branches are then looked up in order
630	        (``name_a`` first): an unknown branch raises :class:`KeyError` and
631	        naming the same branch twice raises :class:`ValueError`; a node
632	        absent from the graph, or outside its named branch's current head
633	        ancestor closure (``node_a`` checked before ``node_b``), raises
634	        :class:`KeyError`. Branch and node checks run even when ``keys``
635	        is empty, in which case an empty tuple is returned.
636	
637	        Every key is answered from one read-only historical view: both
638	        nodes' ancestor closures are taken once before results are built.
639	        The returned tuple has one fresh dict per key, ordered by the
640	        Unicode code point of the keys (independent of their input
641	        order); item-wise, each dict equals the result of
642	        :meth:`attribute_divergence_at` with the same first four
643	        arguments and that key, preserving its key order, types and full
644	        semantics. The dicts and tuples neither share objects with each
645	        other nor alias internal state. Success or failure never modifies
646	        the graph, branch heads, audit or idempotency records.
647	        """
648	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
649	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_a, "node_a")
650	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
651	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_b, "node_b")
652	        if not isinstance(keys, tuple):
653	            raise TypeError(
654	                f"keys must be a tuple, got {type(keys).__name__}"
655	            )
656	        seen_keys: set[str] = set()
657	        for key in keys:
658	            self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
659	            if key in seen_keys:
660	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate key {key!r}")
661	            seen_keys.add(key)
662	
663	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
664	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
665	        if name_a == name_b:
666	            raise ValueError(
667	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
668	                "against itself"
669	            )
670	
671	        # Capture the read-only historical view before any node is
672	        # replayed: the branches' current head closures decide node
673	        # membership, and the nodes' own closures answer every key.
674	        head_closure_a = set(
675	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
676	        )
677	        head_closure_b = set(
678	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
679	        )
680	        if node_a not in self._graph._at or node_a not in head_closure_a:
681	            raise KeyError(node_a)
682	        if node_b not in self._graph._at or node_b not in head_closure_b:
683	            raise KeyError(node_b)
684	
685	        if not keys:
686	            return ()
687	
688	        left_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_a)
689	        right_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_b)
690	        return tuple(
691	            self._attribute_divergence_on_orders(
692	                left_order, right_order, node_a, node_b, key
693	            )
694	            for key in sorted(keys)
695	        )
